title: Win on the channel, not on the product
problem: Our savings product is easy to copy: PhonePe starts at Rs 10 a day and Bachatt already pays agents.
move: Win owners where they already trust someone: trade associations, wholesale markets and suppliers' sales staff. Pay agents for owners still saving after 3 months, not for sign-ups.
how_we_know: Cost per owner still saving at month 3 is Rs 250 or less. Today's evidence is about Rs 500.

title: Make saving fit uneven income: save a slice of the day's takings
problem: A fixed Rs 100 a day fails on slow days. Daily debits fail often, and a third of small daily SIPs stop within a year.
move: Let the daily amount follow the money coming in, for example 2% of yesterday's credits up to a cap. Nobody offers this yet. It needs bank data through a regulated partner, and a lawyer's check on varying amounts under the 24-hour notice rule.
how_we_know: Share still saving at month 12, against a test group on a fixed Rs 100.

title: Sell lenders a better borrower, not a lead
problem: Referral fees are thin, lenders are pulling back, and partner loans are 80% of our revenue.
move: Give each lender a borrower with a saving streak and, with consent, a year of whole-account cash flow. Ask for a higher fee for better loans. Offer first-loss cover, up to the 5% cap, only on loans we pick.
how_we_know: Savers' approval rate, and the share 90+ days late, against each lender's normal book.

title: Prove three numbers in 12 months, then decide on our own book
problem: The plan pays at Rs 250 to win and 1 in 5 borrowing. At today's evidence it does not.
move: Run the pilot on the three pass marks. Start the NBFC application only if losses look like 7.5% a year or less: it takes 8-14 months and Rs 10 crore of capital.
how_we_know: A stop rule to agree now: if a saver still costs over Rs 500 to win and fewer than 1 in 10 borrow after 12 months, stop or change the model. At those numbers the model says each owner loses about Rs 280.
